BackwardScheduler.description:
Backward-pass scheduler and its scheduler-specific parameters
(`config.json → training.parallelism.backward_scheduler`).

The `method` key selects the scheduler, and each scheduler accepts only its
own parameters: a parameter of another scheduler is a load-time error.

oneOf.description:
By-scenario backward scheduling (the default): each parallel work
unit claims one whole trial point (a row of the backward work
rectangle).

By-node backward scheduling: each parallel work unit claims one
(trial point, opening-block) tile of the backward work rectangle.

block_size.description:
Openings per block. Absent resolves per stage to `⌈|Ω_s|/2⌉` (half
the openings, rounded up); a set value is clamped to
`min(|Ω_s|, block_size)`.

BoundaryPolicy.description:
Boundary-row configuration for terminal-stage FCF coupling.

When present, the solver loads rows from a source Novomodelo policy
checkpoint and injects them as fixed boundary conditions at the
terminal stage of the current study. The loader selects the source pool
whose priced state date equals this study's last stage `end_date`.

path.description:
Path to the source policy checkpoint directory (a different study's
output). Resolved relative to the case (input) directory, like every
other input; an absolute path is used as-is. NOT relative to this run's
output directory.

strict.description:
A source slot pricing an entity or commitment this study does not
model is dropped during reconciliation either way. Left `false`, the
drop is recorded in the reconciliation report and the load proceeds;
set `true`, the load is rejected, naming every dropping family and
its count.

CheckpointingConfig.description: Periodic checkpoint settings (`config.json → policy.checkpointing`). Each periodic checkpoint replaces the previous one in the policy directory, so only the latest is kept.

compress.description: Reserved and not read: checkpoint files are written uncompressed whatever its value.

enabled.description: Write periodic checkpoints during training. Off when absent. When true, `interval_iterations` must be at least 1.

initial_iteration.description: Iteration that writes the first periodic checkpoint. Defaults to `interval_iterations`. Iteration numbers are absolute: a resumed run continues the numbering of the run it resumes.

interval_iterations.description: Iterations between periodic checkpoints, counted from `initial_iteration`. Required, and at least 1, when `enabled` is true.

store_basis.description: Reserved and not read: a checkpoint holds the LP bases of the run's scenarios whatever its value.

oneOf.description: Devex approximate edge weights.
Exact steepest-edge weights.
Dantzig most-negative-reduced-cost rule.

EstimationConfig.description:
Time series estimation settings (`config.json → estimation`).

Controls automatic parameter estimation when historical inflow data is
provided without explicit model statistics or coefficients.

max_coefficient_magnitude.description:
Maximum allowed absolute magnitude for any AR coefficient.

When set, any (entity, season) pair with `|coefficient| > threshold`
is immediately reduced to order 0 before the contribution analysis
runs. This acts as a fast-path safety net for the most extreme
explosive models. Absent by default (disabled; contribution analysis
is the primary guard).

max_order.description: Maximum lag order considered during autoregressive model fitting.

min_observations_per_season.description:
Minimum number of observations required per (entity, season) group
to proceed with estimation. Groups below this threshold are skipped.

order_selection.description:
Order selection criterion. Accepts `"pacf"` (classical PACF, default)
or `"pacf_annual"` (PACF augmented with an annual component, PAR(p)-A).

ExportsConfig.description:
Export flags controlling which outputs are written to disk
(`config.json → exports`).

Only the active fields below are accepted. Legacy keys (`training`, `cuts`,
`vertices`, `simulation`, `forward_detail`, `backward_detail`,
`compression`) must be removed from existing `config.json` files before
loading — they are now rejected as unknown fields.

fpha_deviation_points.description:
Export the per-sampled-point computed-FPHA fit-deviation table to
`output/hydro_models/fpha_deviation_points.parquet`.

Opt-in (default `false`) purely for size: it emits one row per
`(hydro, stage, V, Q)` grid point at spillage = 0. Off ⇒ no file and a
byte-identical run; the table is additive and never enters the parity
hash. The values are deterministic (a pure function of geometry + config),
so the file is reproducible when emitted.

states.description:
Store the trial state of each row the run adds, under every selection
method, and write the stored states to the policy checkpoint. Each row
pool that receives rows stores the states of its own rows, at its own
state dimension: the first stage's pool, which keeps every state, and
the pool of each stage strictly between the first and the last, which
under `level1` with `lookback_iterations` keeps only the states inside
the window. A `level1` run stores and writes the states of the pools it
selects whether or not this is set, since a resume reads them. Storing
the states changes no result of the run; the policy then marks its
rows `scored`, which a later `level1` run that loads it selects like
its own rows.

method.description:
Method: `"none"`, `"truncation"`, `"penalty"`, or `"truncation_with_penalty"`.

Default: `"truncation_with_penalty"`. Under `"penalty"` and
`"truncation_with_penalty"` the correction's cost is
`penalties.json → hydro.inflow_nonnegativity_cost` (default 1000.0 when absent);
under `"truncation"` it has no cost.

InflowNonNegativityMethod.description:
Method string for inflow non-negativity enforcement.

Accepted values in `config.json → modeling.inflow_non_negativity.method`:

- `"none"` — no enforcement; the PAR(p) inflow may be negative.
- `"truncation"` — the PAR(p) value stays raw: it is the incremental inflow, and the
  inflow lags of later stages are built from it (aggregated over the lag's period when
  the period spans several stages). A per-hydro correction fixed at `max(−r, 0)`, at no
  cost, lifts the local inflow to zero.
- `"penalty"` — an unbounded correction priced by
  `penalties.json → hydro.inflow_nonnegativity_cost`.
- `"truncation_with_penalty"` — the PAR(p) value stays raw; a correction between 0 and
  `max(−r, 0)`, priced by `penalties.json → hydro.inflow_nonnegativity_cost`.

Under the two truncation methods the correction depends on the incoming state, so the
lower bound can exceed the upper bound, and a `gap` stopping rule can then report
convergence that has not occurred (Larroyd et al. (2022), the paper's §2.5).

oneOf.description: No enforcement; the inflow may be negative.
Raw PAR(p) value; correction fixed at the truncation amount, at no cost.
Unbounded correction priced by `penalties.json → hydro.inflow_nonnegativity_cost`.
Raw PAR(p) value; priced correction capped at the truncation amount.

LipschitzConfig.description: Lipschitz constant settings for inner approximation.

fallback_value.description: Fallback value when automatic computation fails.

scale_factor.description: Multiplicative safety margin applied to computed Lipschitz constants.

cost_scale_factor.description:
Divisor applied to every non-theta objective coefficient at template
build time, multiplied back at every cost-domain reporting boundary.
Default `1_000_000.0` — the value every golden parity baseline is pinned at.

Objective conditioning only — results are identical in exact arithmetic;
this does not alter the model, unlike `modeling`'s other fields. The
effective dual tolerance in currency units is
`dual_feasibility_tolerance × this factor`: raising the factor without
lowering `dual_feasibility_tolerance` proportionally loosens optimality
in currency terms even though the configured tolerance value is
unchanged — the inverse-direction trap a name cannot carry.

Absent uses the default. Must be finite and `> 0`; a value outside
`[1.0, 1e12]` is accepted but logs an advisory warning.

inflow_non_negativity.description: Strategy for handling non-negative inflow constraints.

Openings.description:
Where a stage's openings originate (`config.json` scenario-source `source`).

The tag key is `source` and the field is `openings`, deliberately distinct
from the per-class `scheme` key: `openings.source` selects where a stage's
openings come from, while `scheme` selects how a class's noise is modelled.
A single word would otherwise carry both axes. An absent `openings`
declaration is equivalent to `generated`.

oneOf.description: Openings come from noise generation (the default when `openings` is absent).
Openings come from the conventional `scenarios/noise_openings.parquet` file.

OrderSelectionMethod.description:
Order selection criterion for autoregressive model fitting.

Controls how the lag order is chosen when fitting a time series model.
Two variants are accepted:

- `"pacf"` — classical periodic Yule-Walker with PACF-based order
  selection. Default.
- `"pacf_annual"` — extends `"pacf"` with an annual component (PAR(p)-A),
  adding one extra coefficient ψ per (entity, season) that multiplies
  the rolling 12-month average of past observations.

oneOf.description: Periodic Yule-Walker partial autocorrelation method (PACF).

Periodic Yule-Walker order selection augmented with an annual component.

When selected, the estimation pipeline performs four steps beyond the
classical `pacf` path:

1. **Extended Yule-Walker fitting** — the system is augmented with a
   cross-correlation term between the current-season inflow and the
   rolling 12-month average, yielding the annual coefficient ψ
   alongside the classical AR coefficients.
2. **Annual-stats computation** — per-season sample mean μ^A and
   Bessel-corrected standard deviation σ^A of the rolling 12-month
   average are computed for each hydro plant.
3. **Parquet emission** — the triple (ψ, μ^A, σ^A) is written to
   `inflow_annual_component.parquet` in the output directory.
4. **Widened LP lag stride** — the noise-column layout in the LP is
   extended to accommodate the annual term alongside the classical lags.

ParallelismConfig.description:
Parallel-execution settings (`config.json → training.parallelism`).

Groups the result-preserving knobs that shape how training work is
scheduled across workers, apart from the algorithm-semantics fields at the
`training` root. Thread count itself stays a CLI concern (`--threads`).

PhaseSolverProfileConfig.description:
Per-phase LP solver profile (`config.json → training.solver.backward` /
`.forward`, and `simulation.solver`).

Backend-agnostic. Every field is optional: an absent field leaves the
corresponding option at the phase's built-in tuned-profile value.

presolve.description:
Presolve mode override. Warm-started solves skip presolve regardless
of this setting, so it affects only genuinely cold solves.

simplex_update_limit.description: Simplex update-count limit override before a refactorization.

steepest_edge_devex_fallback_threshold.description:
Dual steepest-edge weight log-error threshold override above which the
solver falls back to Devex pricing.

use_warm_start.description:
Warm-start override. By default backward solves warm-start from the
stored basis and forward and simulation solves are cold.

boundary.description: Optional boundary-row policy for terminal-stage coupling.

mode.description:
Initialization mode: `"fresh"`, `"warm_start"`, or `"resume"`.

A `resume` is refused at load when the checkpoint cannot continue the run as the run that wrote it would have: it was written with another number of forward passes; the run uses `level1` on a study with a stage strictly between the first and the last, and the checkpoint holds no trial-state history, or holds a window while the run keeps every trial state, or holds a shorter window than the run's `lookback_iterations`; the run sets `max_active_per_stage` or the `dynamic` method and the checkpoint holds no binding records; or the run that wrote it ended in an error, which makes it a partial policy. A `warm_start` is not refused for any of these.

path.description:
Policy directory, resolved against the output directory unless absolute. A checkpoint write replaces the whole directory, so an empty path, `.`, `..`, the output directory and its ancestors are refused. So is a directory that names or contains one a run clears before writing its outputs, such as `simulation/solver` or `training/solver`, or that lies inside one a run removes whole, such as `simulation/costs`.

This directory only holds whole checkpoints. A run whose training ends in an error writes its policy to the sibling directory `<path>.partial`, replacing one already there, and leaves this directory as the last whole checkpoint left it; a later run leaves that sibling in place. A run reads the sibling only when `policy.path` names it, and a `resume` of it is refused.

PolicyMode.description:
Policy initialization mode (`config.json → policy.mode`).

Controls whether the training phase starts from scratch, warm-starts from
a prior policy's rows, or resumes a checkpointed training run.

oneOf.description: Start training from an empty future-cost function.
Load rows from a prior policy checkpoint and continue training.

Resume a previously interrupted training run from its checkpoint and
continue it as that run would have continued: the iteration numbering,
each row's role, binding record and stored trial state, and each
scenario's own LP basis are restored.

PresolveMode.description: Presolve mode for a solver profile.

oneOf.description: Presolve enabled.
Presolve disabled.
Solver decides whether to presolve.
Row-wise pricing.
Row-wise pricing with hyper-sparse updates.

RawClassConfigEntry.description: A single per-class scenario scheme in `config.json`.

scheme.description: Forward-pass scenario scheme for this class.

RawHistoricalYearsConfig.description:
`historical_years` in `config.json`: an array of years, such as
`[1940, 1953, 1971]`, or an inclusive range, such as
`{"from": 1940, "to": 2010}`.

oneOf.description: Reuse the backward-pass opening tree for the forward pass.
Draw fresh noise from the same distribution with an independent seed.
Draw from an externally supplied scenario file.
Replay historical realisations.

RawScenarioSourceConfig.description:
Per-class scenario source configuration in `config.json`.

Used by `training.scenario_source` and `simulation.scenario_source`.

historical_years.description: Historical year pool. Absent: the years are discovered at validation time.

inflow.description: Inflow class scenario config. Absent defaults to `in_sample`.

load.description: Load class scenario config. Absent defaults to `in_sample`.

ncs.description: NCS class scenario config. Absent defaults to `in_sample`.

openings.description:
Where a stage's openings come from. Absent defaults to `generated`,
preserving generation-sourced openings.

seed.description: Required when any class uses the `out_of_sample` or `external` scheme.

max_active_per_stage.description:
Cap on the active rows that the current run has added to a stage's row
pool. Absent (default): no cap.

The cap applies to the row pool of every stage strictly between the
first and the last; the pools of the first stage and of the last stage
are not capped. Where the policy graph has several nodes at such a
stage, each node has its own pool and the cap applies to each pool
separately. Rows loaded from a policy (`policy.mode` set to
`warm_start`, or `policy.boundary`) are never evicted and do not count
toward the cap, so a pool can hold more active rows than the cap. Under
`resume` each reloaded row keeps the role it had in the run that wrote
the checkpoint: the rows that run added count toward the cap and can be
evicted, and the rows it loaded do not.

The cap is applied in every training iteration, after that iteration's
rows have been added, whether or not a selection method is configured;
in an iteration where the selection method runs its periodic pass, the
cap is applied after that pass. Rows added in the current iteration
count toward the cap and are never evicted, so the count stays above
the cap when those rows alone exceed it.

When the count exceeds the cap, the excess is evicted from the rows
added in earlier iterations, in ascending order of the iteration in
which a row was last binding; ties go to the row that was binding in
fewer solves, then to the row at the lower position in the pool. A row
that has never been binding ranks by the iteration that added it.
`row_activity_tolerance` decides whether a row is binding.

The cap is rejected at load when set together with
`training.cut_selection.selection.method` = `dynamic` or with
`training.selection.method` set to `enumerated`.

Eviction deactivates a row and keeps it in the pool. With no selection
method an evicted row does not become active again during training.
With `level1`, a later selection pass may reactivate it, and the cap is
then applied again in the same iteration.

row_activity_tolerance.description:
Binding threshold for activity tracking: a constraint row counts as
binding at a solution point when its dual multiplier is strictly greater
than this value (a signed comparison; a multiplier equal to the
threshold does not bind). In one solve the multipliers of a stage's pool
rows are non-negative weights whose sum is at most that stage's discount
factor, so the threshold is dimensionless. The recorded activity is read
only by `max_active_per_stage` and by the `seed_window` of the `dynamic`
method, and it is recorded, and written to the policy checkpoint, only
when one of them is configured. Must be `>= 0`. A value of `0` counts a
multiplier at solver rounding level as binding.

selection.description:
Active selection method and its parameters. Absent/`null` (default)
disables row selection.

oneOf.description: No scaling.
Solver-managed scaling.

SelectionMethod.description:
Row-selection method and its method-specific parameters.

The `method` key selects the method, and each method accepts only its own
parameters: a parameter of another method, a misspelled `method` and a
removed `method` are load-time errors.

oneOf.description:
Level 1: every row the run adds to the row pool of a stage strictly
between the first and the last is scored: the pool stores the trial
state the row was computed at, for the whole run or, with
`lookback_iterations`, for the iterations that key sets. A row loaded
from a policy is scored when the policy records it so (`scored`), which
it does for the rows its writing run added to a pool that stored trial
states, under `level1` or with `exports.states`; the state the policy
holds for such a row, if any, is stored with it. At each stored state,
the row with the highest value there owns the state, among the scored
rows of that pool, active or not, and its other loaded rows that are
active; of rows whose values there are exactly equal, the one at the
lowest pool position owns it. Every `check_frequency` iterations, a
scored row of such a pool is deactivated when it owns no stored state
and reactivated when it is inactive and owns one, also once its own
state has been dropped. Values are compared exactly, with no tolerance,
and a row of the current iteration is judged like any other. A loaded
row that is not scored keeps the activity it was loaded with. Under
`resume` a reloaded row is selected as it would have been in the run
that wrote the checkpoint.

check_frequency.description: Iterations between periodic pruning checks. Default `5`.

lookback_iterations.description:
Iterations of the current run whose rows keep their trial states.
Absent (default): the trial state of every row the run added is
kept, and the memory of a run grows with its row count. A value `w`
keeps the trial states of the rows added in the last `w` iterations
of the current run and drops the older states, never a row: a row
whose state was dropped stays in the pool and still competes at the
states that remain. A state loaded with a row under `warm_start`
counts as one from before the run's first iteration, so it leaves
the window at the run's iteration `w`; under `resume` a reloaded
state leaves it when it would have in the run that wrote the
checkpoint. The memory holding the trial states of a pool is then
bounded by `(lookback_iterations + check_frequency)` times the most
rows the run can add to that pool in one iteration, times the state
dimension, times 8 bytes, plus the states loaded with its rows. Must
be at least `check_frequency`.

oneOf.description:
Dynamic: a per-solve lazy loop, this software's own lazy row generation.
From `start_iteration` on, each training solve starts with the seed rows
described under `seed_window`, adds the candidate rows that its solution
violates, at most `max_added_per_round` per round, and solves again; it
returns when no candidate is violated. After a fixed number of rounds
the per-round limit is lifted. A simulation solve starts with every
active row, so `seed_window` and `candidate_recency` apply to training
only. The method never deactivates a row, and the pool keeps every row.

candidate_recency.description:
Absent (default): every active row is a candidate and a solve returns
the optimum over them. A value `n` restricts the candidates to the
rows added in the last `n` iterations and loaded rows, and the result
is then the optimum over those rows together with the seed rows.
Under `resume` a reloaded row is a loaded row only when the run that
wrote the checkpoint loaded it.

max_added_per_round.description: Maximum rows added per lazy-solve round. Default `10`.

seed_window.description:
A solve starts with the active rows whose last binding was at most
`seed_window` iterations ago (a row that has not bound counts from
the iteration that added it), plus the rows added in the current
iteration. `row_activity_tolerance` decides whether a row binds. `0`
seeds the rows of the current iteration and those that bound in it.
A row loaded from a policy counts from the start of the run under
`warm_start` and for `policy.boundary` rows. Under `resume` a
reloaded row counts as it did in the run that wrote the checkpoint,
which stores each row's binding record. Default `5`.

start_iteration.description: First 1-based iteration at which the lazy loop becomes active. Default `2`.

violation_tolerance.description:
A relative factor: a candidate row is added when its value exceeds
the future-cost value by more than the factor times the larger of
the two magnitudes. Absent (default): each phase uses the primal
feasibility tolerance of its solver profile. A value must be finite
and greater than `0`. It must also be less than 1 and at least the
primal feasibility tolerance of every phase's solver profile.

cut_set.description:
Which rows of each stage's row pool the simulation loads into the stage
LP. `all` loads every row a training run added to the pool, including
rows the selection method deactivated and rows `max_active_per_stage`
evicted, so a simulation LP can be larger than the training LPs.
`active` loads only the rows active when training ended.

A run with training disabled loads each row of the policy with the role
it had in the run that wrote it, so `all` loads what that run's `all`
held and `active` the rows active when it ended; a `resume` does the
same. Under `warm_start` and for `policy.boundary` rows, `all` loads a
row the policy records as `scored` (its writing run stored the trial
state the row was computed at, under `exports.states` or `level1`)
whatever its active flag, and any other loaded row only when that flag
is set. The exported `is_active` flag records the last selection.

A run with `training.cut_selection.selection.method` set to `dynamic`
that simulates under `all` is refused at load when it would hold a row
that `all` includes and that is not active, in the policy it loads under
`warm_start` or `resume` or with training disabled, or in the rows of
`policy.boundary`; set `active`, or use the `level1` method.

io_channel_capacity.description: Bounded channel capacity between simulation threads and the I/O writer thread.

scenario_source.description:
Scenario source configuration for the post-training simulation forward pass.
When absent, falls back to the training scenario source.

selection.description:
Phase-level scenario selection. Absent resolves to the default sampled
count.

solver.description:
Simulation solver profile. Absent leaves the phase's built-in
tuned profile.

SimulationRowSet.description:
The rows of a stage's row pool a simulation loads
(`config.json → simulation.cut_set`).

oneOf.description: Every row a training run added, whatever its active flag.
Only the rows active when training ended.

SimulationSelection.description:
Post-training scenario selection and its method-specific parameters
(`config.json → simulation.selection`).

The `method` key selects how scenarios are chosen: `sampled` draws
`num_scenarios` trajectories; `enumerated` walks the scenario set
exhaustively. Each method accepts only its own parameters, so pairing a
count with `enumerated` is a parse error.

oneOf.description: Sampled scenarios: draw `num_scenarios` trajectories.

num_scenarios.description: Number of simulation trajectories to draw.

oneOf.description: Exhaustive enumeration of the scenario set.

StoppingMode.description:
How multiple stopping rules combine into a single stop decision
(`config.json → training.stopping_mode`).

oneOf.description: Stop when any configured rule triggers (OR).

Stop when every configured rule other than `iteration_limit` triggers at
the same iteration (AND); the largest `iteration_limit` caps the run.

StoppingRuleConfig.description: One entry of `training.stopping_rules`. The `type` key selects the rule; a key that belongs to another rule type is a load-time error.

oneOf.description:
Stop after a fixed number of iterations. **Mandatory** — every rule set must
contain at least one `iteration_limit` rule.
Stop after a wall-clock time limit.
Stop when the lower bound stalls (relative improvement falls below tolerance).

iterations.description: Window size (number of past iterations to compare).

oneOf.description:
Stop when the exact upper bound is within tolerance of the lower
bound. At least one of `tolerance` / `relative_tolerance` must be
present (checked at `from_config`). Admissible only under enumerated
forward selection, where the upper bound is the exact bound a gap rule
requires rather than a statistical estimate.

relative_tolerance.description:
Relative gap tolerance in percent (e.g. `0.01` means 0.01%), compared
against `100·gap / max(1, |lower_bound|)` — the same convention the
reported `gap_percent` uses.

TrainingConfig.description:
Training parameters (`config.json → training`).

`selection` and `stopping_rules` are required; the loader rejects a
configuration that omits either.

enabled.description: Enable the training phase. When `false`, skip directly to simulation.

scenario_source.description:
Scenario source configuration for the training forward pass.
When absent, all classes default to `in_sample`.

selection.description:
Phase-level scenario selection. The forward-pass count lives in the
`sampled` arm; absent is a missing-count load error.

oneOf.description: Sampled forward passes: `forward_passes` trajectories per iteration.

forward_passes.description: Number of forward-pass trajectories per iteration.

oneOf.description: Exhaustive enumeration of the scenario openings.

solver.description: LP solver retry settings and optional per-phase solver profiles.

stopping_mode.description:
How multiple stopping rules combine: `any` (OR) or `all` (AND over every
rule except `iteration_limit`, which caps the run).

stopping_rules.description:
List of stopping rule configurations.

**Mandatory** — no default. Must contain at least one `iteration_limit` rule.

tree_seed.description: Random seed for the opening scenario tree (reproducible training).

TrainingSolverConfig.description:
LP solver settings (`config.json → training.solver`): retry policy plus
optional per-phase solver profiles.

backward.description:
Backward-pass solver profile. Absent leaves the phase's built-in
tuned profile.

forward.description:
Forward-pass solver profile. Absent leaves the phase's built-in
tuned profile.

retry_max_attempts.description: Maximum solver retry attempts before propagating a hard error.

retry_time_budget_seconds.description: Total time budget in seconds across all retry attempts for one solve.

enabled.description: Enable vertex-based inner approximation for upper bound computation.

initial_iteration.description: First iteration to compute the upper bound.

description:
Root object of `config.json`.

Every section except `training` is optional; an absent section takes its defaults.

$schema.description: JSON schema URI — informational, not validated.

estimation.description: Time series estimation settings for automatic model parameter fitting.

exports.description: Export flags controlling which outputs are written to disk.

title: Config
